executive_summary.headline: Hyperscalers will spend $500B+ through 2027, concentrating capacity in five power-rich regions
bullets: AI training drives ~60% of incremental capex; inference workloads scale 4x by 2027
Power capacity is the binding constraint; new builds shift to TX, IA, ND, Quebec, and Riyadh
Top 4 hyperscalers control 78% of cloud spend; colocation share drops below 25% by 2027

slides.action_title: Global cloud infrastructure spend grows from $200B to $500B+ through 2027, a 17% CAGR
commentary: AI training drives the acceleration: spend rises from $70B (2024) to $260B (2027), surpassing non-AI cloud capex
Inference workloads grow 4x by 2027 as enterprise adoption scales beyond pilots
Hyperscale absorbs 85% of incremental spend; colocation share contracts to ~25% by 2027
Liquid cooling moves from optional to mandatory; 70% of new hyperscale builds spec it by 2026
slides.footnote: Hyperscale defined as AWS, Azure, GCP, Meta, Oracle, and Alibaba combined.
slides.source: Synergy Research Group, 2024; JLL Data Center Outlook, 2024; IDC Worldwide AI Infrastructure Tracker, 2024

slides.action_title: Top 4 hyperscalers control 78% of cloud spend; AWS leads but Azure and GCP gain share each year

chart.unit: Percentage share of global cloud infrastructure spend

commentary.text: AWS: share compressed 33% → 32% over two years; absolute dollars still grow ~25% YoY
Azure: adds ~1pp annually; OpenAI exclusivity and enterprise integration are the wedges
Google Cloud: AI services drive incremental share against AWS general-purpose lead

slides.source: Synergy Research Group Cloud Infrastructure Quarterly, 2024

slides.action_title: Colocation remains fragmented: top 5 hold just 35% combined, with Equinix and Digital Realty leading

chart.unit: Percentage share of global colocation revenue*

commentary.text: Equinix: leads on retail interconnection and brand premium; trades at ~28x EBITDA
Digital Realty: leads on hyperscale wholesale; trades at ~22x EBITDA
Tier-2 metros (Atlanta, Dallas, Phoenix) are the consolidation battleground for 2026

slides.footnote: Top 5 combined; remaining 65% split across 200+ regional and specialty providers.

slides.action_title: Hyperscalers move toward self-build for AI; colocation pivots to enterprise hybrid and AI startups

left.text: Self-build AI campuses to capture full margin and control power, cooling, and supply chain
Vertical integration: custom silicon (Trainium, TPU, Maia), networking, optical interconnect
Multi-region power deals: nuclear PPAs, gigawatt-scale wind and solar contracts

right.text: Enterprise hybrid: 60% of revenue from financial services, healthcare, and government
AI startup foundry: powered shells with pre-installed liquid cooling for unicorn customers
Edge expansion: tier-2 metros where hyperscalers underbuild, locking in latency-sensitive customers

slides.source: JLL Data Center Outlook, 2024; company earnings filings

slides.action_title: Five regions absorb 70% of new capacity; the US heartland sees the largest acceleration

commentary.text: Dominion paused new high-density requests in 2024; North VA queue stretches 7+ years
Hydro-Quebec is the cleanest power option: 95% hydro grid attractive for AI training
MidAmerican (Iowa) attracts hyperscalers via long-term clean-power PPAs
Constellation-Microsoft deal sets the SMR/nuclear-restart template for 2027 unlock
ERCOT (Texas) leads on speed: 18-month interconnect for projects under 200MW
PIF (Saudi sovereign wealth fund) backs Riyadh: capital-rich, queue-light, gas-heavy

slides.footnote: Power, not land or fiber, is now the binding constraint; interconnect queues range from 4 to 7 years.
slides.source: JLL Data Center Outlook, 2024; ERCOT Capacity Outlook, 2024; Hydro-Quebec Industrial Customer Briefing, 2024

recommendations.headline: Build NYAL data center exposure in Texas and Quebec; partner with colocation incumbents in tier-2 metros

actions.action: Issue term sheets for two TX powered-shell sites by 2026-09; target 50MW each
actions.outcome: Texas footprint locked ahead of 2027 demand peak

actions.action: Negotiate Hydro-Quebec PPA with anchor tenant (Anthropic or OpenAI) by 2026-12
Sign MSAs with Equinix and Digital Realty for tier-2 metro colocation by 2026-08
actions.outcome: Coverage in 12 metros without capex commitment

actions.action: Raise $1.2B preferred equity for AI-campus development by 2026-11

appendix.action_title: Methodology: market sizing reconciles four data sources and a NYAL-built power-availability model
bullets: Cloud infrastructure spend reconciled across Synergy Research, IDC, Dell'Oro, and Gartner; 2024 baseline within +/- 4%
Colocation share derived from Structure Research census plus public 10-Ks for top 10 providers
Regional capacity figures triangulated from JLL, Dgtl Infra, and ERCOT/Hydro-Quebec interconnect filings
Power-availability model: 12-month rolling queue depth across 18 ISOs, mapped to hyperscaler RFP windows

appendix.action_title: Detailed hyperscaler capex by year: AWS leads in absolute dollars, Microsoft accelerates fastest in 2025-2027

chart.unit: USD billions, annual data center and AI capex

commentary.text: Microsoft surpasses AWS in 2025 incremental capex; OpenAI partnership drives the gap
Meta's 2024-2025 inflection reflects the pivot to in-house AI (Llama, AI Studio, Reels recommender)
Google's slower growth reflects GCP's smaller share, not strategic restraint

appendix.footnote: Includes both data center construction and AI accelerator purchases; excludes traditional R&D.
appendix.source: Company 10-Ks and quarterly capex disclosures, NYAL analysis, 2026
